sentences.text:
Sheru Khan vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 6 February,
2025
 Neutral Citation No. 2025:Mphc-Jbp:5754
 1 
 In The High Court Of Madhya Pradesh

Before
 Hon'Ble Shri Justice Devnarayan Mishra

On The 6 th Of February, 2025
 Misc. Criminal Case No. 1436 of 2025
 Sheru Khan
 Versus
 The State Of Madhya Pradesh And Others
 Appearance:
 Shri Avinash Raizada - Advocate for the applicant.
 Shri Manoj Jha - Panel Lawyer for respondent/State.

Order 
This is the first application filed by the applicant under Section 483 of Bhartiya Nagrik Suraksha Sanhita , 2023/Section 439 of Cr.P.C., 1973 for grant of regular bail relating to FIR/Crime No.249/2024 registered at Police Station - Kohefiza, District - Bhopal (M.P.) for the offence punishable under Sections 376(AB), 376(2)(n), 376(2)(f) and 506 of the IPC and Sections 5(L)/6,
5(n)/6 and 5(n)/6 of the POCSO Act.
2. Learned counsel for applicant has submitted that the applicant has been falsely implicated in the case.
The victim has filed report when the family members saw the incident and the applicant has also dispute with his wife.
On that basis, report has been lodged.
Trial will take time to be concluded.
Hence, the applicant be released on bail.
3. Learned counsel for State has opposed the bail application and has submitted that FSL and DNA reports are awaited but looking to the offence, the applicant is not entitled to be released on bail.
Heard the parties and perused the case diary.
5. In this case, the victim was of 14 years of age and when the offence was committed she must be 9 to 10 years and the applicant is father of the victim.

6. Looking to the above facts and circumstances but without commenting on the merit of the case,
the bail application is dismissed.
